content: Celiac disease is observed to be more prevalent among youth diagnosed with type 1 diabetes, with a reported prevalence ranging from approximately 1% to 16%. Screening for celiac disease antibodies, specifically tissue transglutaminase IgA (tTG IgA) and total serum IgA, is recommended at the time of type 1 diabetes diagnosis. This screening should be repeated if the individual develops symptoms suggestive of celiac disease or if there is a family history of the condition in first-degree relatives. For individuals diagnosed with celiac disease, adherence to a strict gluten-free diet is essential to manage symptoms and to prevent potential complications associated with the condition. It is strongly advised that these individuals work closely with a registered dietitian who has expertise in managing both diabetes and celiac disease to ensure optimal dietary management and overall health outcomes.
